title: No-signaling values of quantum games--an operator algebra perspective
authors: Roy Araiza, Marius Junge, Carlos Palazuelos
abstract: The aim of this work is to study two-prover quantum games (i.e., games with quantum inputs and outputs) from an operator-algebraic and operator-space point of view. We characterize several notions of the value of such games by formulating them in terms of tensor norms in the category of operator spaces. The main results of the paper concern the description of the so-called no-signalling value of these games, for which we not only provide a precise operator-space formulation, but also establish close connections between this study and some problems in operator algebras. In particular, we show how the recent counterexample to Grothendieck's theorem for operator spaces given in \cite{Ara} can be understood as a direct consequence of results in quantum information theory. We also obtain new upper bounds on the gap between the no-signalling value and the quantum value of two-prover quantum games, improving the best previously known estimates.
summary: This paper provides a deep operator algebraic characterization of 'no-signalling' constraints in two-prover quantum games. It defines and relates several quantitative measures ($\omega_{NOS}$ and $\omega_{SNOS}$) using sophisticated tensor norms from functional analysis. The results connect quantum information theory directly to unsolved problems in the structure theory of operator algebras.
main_problem: The work aims to rigorously characterize the 'no-signalling value' ($\omega_{NOS}(G)$) of two-prover quantum games by reformulating these concepts using advanced tools from operator space theory and tensor norms.
main_result: The authors establish deep connections between $\omega_{NOS}(G)$ and a related sub-no-signalling value ($\omega_{SNOS}(G)$), proving bounds like $\omega_{NOS}(G) \le \omega_{SNOS}(G) \le 8 \cdot \omega_{NOS}(G)$, while also connecting these values to open problems in operator algebras.
method: The methodology heavily relies on functional analysis, specifically utilizing various tensor norms (e.g., $\min$, $\mu$) within the framework of operator spaces and analyzing completely positive trace-preserving maps via their Choi matrices.
model_or_system: The model is abstract: two-prover quantum games ($G$), which are mathematically analyzed using tensors defined over state spaces ($\mathcal{S}_1(\cdot)$) associated with input and output systems for the players (Alice and Bob).
key_observables: No-signalling value ($\omega_{NOS}(G)$), sub-no-signalling value ($\omega_{SNOS}(G)$), and various tensor norms quantifying game values.
important_parameters: The analysis involves comparing constants derived from different norm estimates, such as $c_1$ and $c_2$, and the rank of associated tensors ($	ext{rank}(\eta_G)$).
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on advanced theorems regarding operator spaces (e.g., Pisier's results) and specific structural assumptions about how quantum strategies map between input/output systems.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining game values using tensor norms, then establishing equivalences between different types of quantum strategies (e.g., one-way vs. no-signalling), and finally deriving quantitative bounds relating the various defined 'no-signalling' measures.
why_interesting: This work is highly theoretical but relevant to open questions in quantum information theory, particularly concerning the fundamental limitations imposed by causality (no-signaling) when quantifying correlations in multipartite quantum systems.
